fr:title.text: Theme Studio — the current forest theme

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Theme Studio — the current forest theme

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Reference for the theme currently shipping on this forest — the Theme Studio redesign (April 2026). Supersedes the earlier theming note Forest Theming Customization, which describes the upstream base theme plus a thin Dracula overlay and is no longer accurate. Background on why theming lives in a fork at all is in Forking Forester.

The theme is a git submodule at ~/forest/theme/, declared in .gitmodules. The submodule URL points to a personal fork — git@github.com:stschaef/forester-base-theme.git — not the upstream Sourcehut repo. The fork tracks upstream's 4.3.0 tag as its base, with Theme Studio commits layered on top.
Inside the submodule, the live remotes are:

html:ul.html:li: origin → https://git.sr.ht/~jonsterling/forester-base-theme (read-only upstream, for pulling new releases)
fork → git@github.com:stschaef/forester-base-theme.git (read/write, what the submodule actually checks out)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The forest repo records a commit SHA in the theme submodule; the build configs (forest.toml, public.toml) point Forester at theme/ for XSL templates and at theme/style.css, theme/forester.js, theme/forester-extras.js for the bundled assets. Forester copies these into output/ on each build.
Key files inside the submodule:

html:ul.html:li: style.css — ~930 lines, the entire Theme Studio palette (see theme architecture)
style.css.upstream-bak — preserved copy of the pre-redesign upstream CSS, kept for reference
forester-extras.js — the persistent left rail builder, kept separate so re-bundling forester.js from upstream sources doesn't clobber it
forester.js — bundled from javascript-source/forester.js via bundle-js.sh (esbuild)
tree.xsl, default.xsl, core.xsl, links.xsl, metadata.xsl — XSL pipeline, near-upstream
themes/dracula.css — legacy single-overlay file from before the redesign; superseded by inline theme blocks in style.css, kept around but no longer wired up
fonts/ — only KaTeX fonts; body/heading fonts now come from the system stack or web fonts loaded by name (Newsreader, Jost)

fr:title.text: Theme Studio architecture — six themes via token overrides

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Theme Studio architecture — six themes via token overrides

fr:mainmatter.html:p: style.css defines one set of base design tokens on :root (colors, fonts, spacing, taxon stamp palette, TODO state colors) and six themes that override those tokens. Each theme is dispatched by \meta{theme}{X}, which the XSL pipeline turns into article.theme-X; the override block lives on :root:has(article.theme-X) so the tokens flow through the whole document, not just the article.
The six themes:

html:ul.html:li: paper — Field Notes inspired; burnt orange · burgundy · slate blue · mustard on cream; Newsreader serif body, Jost display
dracula — refined dark; the original overlay, now folded into the unified file
academic — high-contrast scholarly light; Newsreader throughout, italic small-caps taxons
solarized — Ethan Schoonover's warm-neutral palette
editorial — Swiss / bold Helvetica with vermilion accent and heavy display sizes
blueprint — ice-on-navy dark variant with a faint grid backdrop on body

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Beyond the token block, each theme adds a small set of theme-internal flourishes via article.theme-X selectors — depth-cycled subtree border colors in paper, the grid background in blueprint, italic emphasis recolor in dracula, etc.
The default theme is paper, set as an XSL variable in tree.xsl:
When a tree omits \meta{theme}, the XSL falls back to this default; \meta{theme}{none} explicitly opts out (no theme class is emitted, base tokens win).

Theme dispatch is entirely in theme/tree.xsl, around lines 76–87. The XSL writes a class attribute on .tree-container computed from \meta{theme}{...}:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: <xsl:choose> <xsl:when test="...meta[@name='theme'] = 'none'" /> <xsl:when test="...meta[@name='theme']"> <xsl:text> theme-</xsl:text> <xsl:value-of select="...meta[@name='theme']" /> </xsl:when> <xsl:when test="$default-theme != ''"> <xsl:text> theme-</xsl:text> <xsl:value-of select="$default-theme" /> </xsl:when> </xsl:choose>
fr:mainmatter.html:p: Three cases:

html:ul.html:li: Tree sets \meta{theme}{X} → emits class="... theme-X", which activates the matching :root:has(article.theme-X) block in style.css
Tree sets \meta{theme}{none} → no theme class; base :root tokens win (academic-light fallback)
No theme meta → falls through to $default-theme (currently paper)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: To add a new theme, the workflow is: pick a name, add a :root:has(article.theme-<name>) { ... } block in style.css overriding the relevant tokens, and optionally a few article.theme-<name> selectors for theme-specific structural touches. No XSL or compiler change needed.
To change the site-wide default, edit the $default-theme variable at the top of tree.xsl.

The XSL still emits layout-X classes on both grid-wrapper and .tree-container when a tree sets \meta{layout}{X} (see tree.xsl:63-75), but the Theme Studio style.css has zero .layout-* rules. So \meta{layout}{wide}, dashboard, table, kanban all attach a class that styles nothing.

The upstream-backup CSS (theme/style.css.upstream-bak) had twelve .layout-* rules covering layout-wide, layout-table, layout-kanban. None of them survived the Theme Studio rewrite. layout-dashboard was never styled even in the upstream version — the dashboard layout described in the forest CLAUDE.md was aspirational.
Trees that still set \meta{layout}{wide} (the index, dashboard, a few public refs) render exactly as if the meta were absent. Either:

html:ul.html:li: Port the relevant rules out of style.css.upstream-bak into style.css, or
Strip the now-meaningless \meta{layout} declarations from the trees that set them

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The CLAUDE.md doc still lists \meta{layout}{wide|dashboard|table|kanban} as a supported customization surface; that section needs updating in lockstep with whichever fix lands.
Editing the theme means editing the submodule. The flow:

html:ul.html:li: Edit style.css, forester-extras.js, or whichever file
git commit inside theme/ (the commit lands on the fork remote's branch)
git push fork to publish
Back in ~/forest: git add theme then git commit to bump the recorded submodule SHA

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Forgetting the second commit means the forest repo still points at the old theme SHA — locally everything looks right, but other clones (and forest-pull.service on the home server) will check out the stale version.
For local iteration, ./server.sh runs Forester in dev mode with fswatch on both trees/ and theme/; CSS edits hot-rebuild without touching git at all. Only commit when the change is settled.
To pull in upstream Forester theme releases:

html:ul.html:li: Inside theme/: git fetch origin
git merge <upstream-tag> or rebase the Theme Studio commits onto the new tag
Expect conflicts in style.css and tree.xsl — these are the most heavily modified files
forester-extras.js should never conflict (upstream doesn't know about it)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The whole subsystem assumes you also have read access to ~/ocaml-forester for reference — when an XSL change behaves unexpectedly, the upstream compiler source (lib/frontend/Htmx_client.ml, lib/parser/) is the authoritative explanation of what classes and attributes the pipeline emits.
